name: Plesetsk Site 43
tagline: Plesetsk's workhorse Soyuz pad at 62.9°N — the world's highest-latitude active orbital launch complex
description: Plesetsk Cosmodrome sits at 62.9°N — the world's highest-latitude active orbital launch complex. Site 43 is one of several pads at Plesetsk and operates Soyuz-2 today for Russian polar / Molniya / GLONASS payloads. Originally an R-7 ICBM base in the late 1950s, repurposed for space launches in 1966, and for several decades Plesetsk held the record for most orbital launches from any single site on Earth. The high latitude limits how much the Earth's rotation contributes (less than at Baikonur or Wenchang), but it's perfect for high-inclination missions that Baikonur can't easily reach without dogleg manoeuvres.
best_known_for: World's most northerly orbital launch site — Russia's polar / Molniya military + GLONASS pad
